title: CASB API, SDK and Terraform surface

prose.text: This subject is the API shape of CASB; behavior is in the subjects it points to.

prose.label: Tenant calls.
prose.text: {{tenant-read-endpoints}} {{tenant-list-filters}} {{snake-case-wrappers}} {{scan-info-paging}} {{scan-info-members}} Tenant behavior is in [[zia.casb.tenants]] and scan behavior in [[zia.casb.scans]].

prose.label: Rule calls.
prose.text: {{rule-endpoints}} How `ruleType` scopes them is in [[zia.casb.rule-types:ruletype-scoped-calls]]. {{go-rule-reads}} Paging pitfalls for ZIA lists are in [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination]].

prose.label: Helper lists.
prose.text: {{helper-lite-endpoints}} {{go-domain-profiles-unlisted}} {{python-domain-profiles-lite}} The SDKs disagree on which list to read {{divergence:domain-profiles-endpoint}}.

prose.label: SDKs.
prose.text: {{python-clients}} The enabled-to-state conversion for CASB DLP rules is covered with the other rule modules in [[zia.sdk-python.request-conventions:enabled-to-state-more-modules]].

prose.label: Terraform.
prose.text: {{terraform-resources}} {{terraform-import-and-target}} The order, contiguity and predefined-rule constraints are in [[zia.casb.dlp-rules:order-contract]] and [[zia.casb.malware-rules:malware-order-contract]]; the shared registry defect is in [[zia.terraform.rule-order.registry:casb-rules-one-key-for-all-types]], and the field defects in [[zia.terraform.field-fidelity]].

checks.do: Whether a tenant filter uses the API camelCase name when it is written outside Terraform and the Python SDK.
Whether a Go SDK rule list for one type is a single read, and use GetAll for the complete set.
Whether domain profile attributes came from the lite list or the full list before comparing SDKs.

tenant-read-endpoints.statement: The documented tenant calls are all GET: the tenant list `casbTenant/lite`, scan configuration `casbTenant/scanInfo`, validation status `casbTenant/validate/status/{tenantId}`, and the policy tags `casbTenant/{tenantId}/tags/policy`.

expect.description: Retrieves information about the SaaS application tenant. .
Retrieves the SaaS Security Scan Configuration information. .
Retrieves the validation status of the SaaS application tenant based on the tenant ID
Retrieves the tags used in the policy rules associated with a tenant, based on the tenant ID.

tenant-list-filters.statement: The tenant list filters use camelCase names (`activeOnly`, `includeDeleted`, `scanConfigTenantsOnly`, `includeBucketReadyS3Tenants`, `filterByFeature`, `appType`, `app`, `page`, `pageSize`), and `activeOnly` defaults to true.

expect.description: Indicates that the tenant is in use. Policies are enforced for this SaaS application.
Specifies the tenant for which the scan is already configured
For the AWS S3 SaaS application, this parameter indicates that the buckets have been read and are ready for use in policies and scan configurations.

snake-case-wrappers.statement: The Python SDK documents the tenant filters as snake_case (`active_only`, `scan_config_tenants_only`, `filter_by_feature`) and the Terraform data source takes the same snake_case arguments, while the Go SDK passes the caller's keys through unchanged.

quotes: ``[query_params.active_only]`` {bool}: Indicates that the tenant is in use.
``[query_params.scan_config_tenants_only]`` {bool}: Specifies the tenant which the scan is already configured
(Boolean) Specifies the tenant for which the scan is already configured

scan-info-paging.statement: The scan information and tenant policy tags calls page with `page` (default 1) and `pageSize` (default 500); the tenant list declares no defaults, and the Go SDK reads all three through its all-pages helper.

expect.description: Specifies the page size
Specifies the page size

scan-info-members.statement: The Go SDK reads scan information as the tenant name, tenant ID, SaaS application, an integer `scanAction`, and a `scanInfo` object with `cur_scan_start_time`, `prev_scan_end_time` and `scan_reset_num`; the OpenAPI document declares `scanInfo` as an object with no members.

expect.description: The scan configuration information

rule-endpoints.statement: Each rule kind has the same endpoint set: create and list at `/casbDlpRules` and `/casbMalwareRules`, list everything at `/all`, and get, update and delete at `/{ruleId}`.

helper-lite-endpoints.statement: Three helper lists are read-only `lite` calls: domain profiles (`/domainProfiles/lite`), quarantine tombstone templates (`/quarantineTombstoneTemplate/lite`) and CASB email labels (`/casbEmailLabel/lite`).

go-domain-profiles-unlisted.statement: The Go SDK reads domain profiles from `/domainProfiles`, which its source comments as publicly available but absent from the swagger, and comments out the `/domainProfiles/lite` endpoint because it misses important attributes.

quotes: // Endpoint is publicly available but not present in the swagger

python-domain-profiles-lite.statement: The Python SDK reads domain profiles from `/domainProfiles/lite`.

go-rule-reads.statement: In the Go SDK, `GetByRuleType` and `GetByRuleID` make a single read for one rule type, while `GetAll` pages through `/all` with the all-pages helper; Update sends the rule to `/{id}` with no `ruleType`, and Delete requires the rule type.

python-clients.statement: The Python SDK has a client class for each of the DLP rules (`CasbdDlpRulesAPI`), the malware rules (`CasbMalwareRulesAPI`) and the tenant, scan and helper calls (`SaaSSecurityAPI`).

terraform-resources.statement: Terraform has resources `zia_casb_dlp_rules` and `zia_casb_malware_rules`, and read-only data sources `zia_casb_tenant`, `zia_casb_tombstone_template` and `zia_casb_email_label`.

data source to get information about templates for the tombstone file created when a file is quarantined
data source to get information about email labels generated for the SaaS Security API policies

terraform-import-and-target.statement: A CASB rule imports with `<RULE_TYPE:RULE_ID>` or `<RULE_TYPE:RULE_NAME>` as the import ID, and a custom rule is removed by pointing Terraform's `-target` flag at it.

quotes: can be imported by using `<RULE_TYPE:RULE_ID>` or `<RULE_TYPE:RULE_NAME>` as the import ID.
When deleting existing custom rules, use the Terraform `-target` flag to target the specific rule to be removed.

domain-profiles-endpoint.summary: The OpenAPI document and the Python SDK use the domain profile `lite` list; the Go SDK reads `/domainProfiles` instead.

expect.description: Retrieves the domain profile summary. To learn more about domain profiles, navigate to the 'Domain Profiles' section from .

positions.says: Only `/domainProfiles/lite` is documented, and it returns the domain profile summary.
The `lite` endpoint misses important attributes, so the SDK reads the full `/domainProfiles` list, which the swagger does not list.

domain-profiles-endpoint.impact: A client built from the OpenAPI document sees a smaller domain profile than the Go SDK returns, so profile attributes seen through one are not evidence for the other.
